question: Who directed the 1968 film '2001: A Space Odyssey'?
explanation: Stanley Kubrick directed 2001: A Space Odyssey (1968), co-writing the screenplay with science fiction author Arthur C. Clarke based on Clarke's short story 'The Sentinel.' The film is widely regarded as one of the greatest films ever made, pioneering special effects techniques and profoundly influencing the science fiction genre.

question: Which film won the first ever Academy Award for Best Picture?
choices: All Quiet on the Western Front
explanation: Wings (1927), a World War I aerial combat film directed by William Wellman, won the first Academy Award for Outstanding Picture (later renamed Best Picture) at the inaugural ceremony in 1929. Sunrise: A Song of Two Humans also won a special 'Unique and Artistic Picture' award at that same ceremony, causing some confusion, but Wings won the standard Best Picture prize.

question: In which film did Marlon Brando play Vito Corleone?
explanation: Marlon Brando played Vito Corleone, the aging patriarch of the Corleone mafia family, in Francis Ford Coppola's The Godfather (1972), winning the Academy Award for Best Actor (which he famously declined). The role required extensive prosthetic work and a distinctive raspy voice Brando developed for the character.

question: What is the name of the fictional African country in Black Panther?
explanation: Wakanda is the fictional African nation in Marvel Comics and the MCU film Black Panther (2018) — a technologically advanced kingdom that has hidden its wealth of the fictional metal vibranium from the world. Zamunda is from Coming to America, Genovia is from The Princess Diaries, and Latveria is the fictional nation of Doctor Doom in Marvel Comics.

question: Which actress plays Clarice Starling in The Silence of the Lambs?
explanation: Jodie Foster played FBI trainee Clarice Starling in The Silence of the Lambs (1991), winning the Academy Award for Best Actress for the role. The film became one of only three films to win all five major Oscar categories (Picture, Director, Actor, Actress, Screenplay), and Foster's performance opposite Anthony Hopkins as Hannibal Lecter is considered one of cinema's great pairings.

question: Who wrote the novel that the film 'No Country for Old Men' is based on?
explanation: No Country for Old Men was a 2005 novel by Cormac McCarthy, adapted into the 2007 Coen Brothers film that won four Academy Awards including Best Picture. McCarthy is known for his dark, violent prose and novels such as Blood Meridian and The Road, all dealing with themes of fate, violence, and moral ambiguity in American landscapes.

question: What year was the first Star Wars film released?
explanation: Star Wars (later subtitled A New Hope) was released on May 25, 1977, directed by George Lucas, and became the highest-grossing film of all time at that point. It spawned one of the most successful media franchises in history; The Empire Strikes Back followed in 1980, and Return of the Jedi in 1983.

question: Which country produced the film 'Parasite', winner of the 2020 Best Picture Oscar?
explanation: Parasite (2019), directed by Bong Joon-ho, was a South Korean film that made history at the 2020 Academy Awards by becoming the first non-English language film to win Best Picture, along with three other Oscars. It is a darkly comedic thriller about class inequality and is widely considered one of the best films of the 21st century.

question: Who plays Tony Soprano in 'The Sopranos'?
explanation: James Gandolfini played Tony Soprano, the New Jersey mob boss and central character of The Sopranos, in all six seasons (1999–2007). Gandolfini won three Emmy Awards for the role, which is widely considered one of the greatest performances in television history. Michael Imperioli played his nephew Christopher Moltisanti.

question: In 'Blade Runner', what are the human-like robots called?
explanation: In Blade Runner (1982), the bioengineered humanoids are called Replicants — beings nearly indistinguishable from humans, created by the Tyrell Corporation for labor in off-world colonies. The term comes from the source novel Do Androids Dream of Electric Sheep? by Philip K. Dick. 'Synths' are from Fallout, and 'Cylons' are from Battlestar Galactica.

question: Which director made 'Schindler's List', 'Jurassic Park', and 'Saving Private Ryan'?
explanation: Steven Spielberg directed all three films: Schindler's List (1993) and Saving Private Ryan (1998) each won him Academy Awards for Best Director, and Jurassic Park (1993) was a landmark in visual effects. He released Schindler's List and Jurassic Park in the same year (1993), a remarkable achievement demonstrating his range from blockbuster entertainment to profound historical drama.

question: What is the highest-grossing film of all time (not adjusted for inflation)?
explanation: Avatar (2009), directed by James Cameron, is the highest-grossing film of all time with over $2.9 billion in worldwide box office revenue, a title it regained after its 2021 re-release following a brief period when Avengers: Endgame held the record. Avatar (2022), the sequel, also became one of the highest-grossing films ever made.

question: In 'Breaking Bad', what is Walter White's teacher alias?
explanation: Walter White adopts the alias 'Heisenberg' in Breaking Bad, a reference to physicist Werner Heisenberg, who formulated the Heisenberg Uncertainty Principle in quantum mechanics. The alias reflects Walter's transformation from a mild-mannered chemistry teacher into a ruthless drug lord, invoking the name of a scientist who also worked in morally ambiguous territory (Heisenberg worked on Germany's nuclear program in WWII).

question: Which film features the line 'You can't handle the truth!'?
explanation: The iconic line 'You can't handle the truth!' is delivered by Jack Nicholson as Colonel Nathan Jessup during the climactic courtroom interrogation scene in A Few Good Men (1992), directed by Rob Reiner. The screenplay was written by Aaron Sorkin, based on his own Broadway play, and the scene opposite Tom Cruise became one of cinema's most quoted moments.

question: Who plays Hannibal Lecter in 'The Silence of the Lambs'?
explanation: Anthony Hopkins played Dr. Hannibal Lecter in The Silence of the Lambs (1991), winning the Academy Award for Best Actor despite having only about 16 minutes of screen time — one of the shortest performances ever to win that award. Brian Cox notably played Lecter (spelled Lecktor) in the earlier film Manhunter (1986), based on the same character.

question: Which TV show features the fictional paper company Dunder Mifflin?
explanation: Dunder Mifflin Paper Company is the fictional Scranton, Pennsylvania-based paper supply company at the center of The Office (US version, 2005–2013), based on Ricky Gervais's British original. The show was a mockumentary following the mundane office life of regional manager Michael Scott (Steve Carell) and his employees.

question: Who directed 'Pulp Fiction'?
explanation: Quentin Tarantino wrote and directed Pulp Fiction (1994), which won the Palme d'Or at Cannes and was nominated for seven Academy Awards, winning one for Original Screenplay. The film's non-linear structure, sharp dialogue, and mix of dark humor with violence redefined independent cinema and cemented Tarantino as one of his generation's most influential filmmakers.

question: What is the name of the bar in 'Cheers'?
explanation: The bar in the sitcom Cheers is simply called 'Cheers,' based on a real Boston bar called The Bull & Finch Pub (now renamed 'Cheers' itself due to the show's popularity). The show ran from 1982 to 1993 and is set in a Boston basement bar where 'everybody knows your name.'

question: In which year was the first episode of 'Game of Thrones' broadcast?
explanation: Game of Thrones premiered on HBO on April 17, 2011, based on George R.R. Martin's A Song of Ice and Fire novel series. The show went on to run for eight seasons until 2019 and became one of the most watched television series in history, winning a record 59 Primetime Emmy Awards over its run.

question: Which actress played Katniss Everdeen in The Hunger Games?
explanation: Jennifer Lawrence played Katniss Everdeen across all four Hunger Games films (2012–2015), based on Suzanne Collins's trilogy. Lawrence was already an Oscar-nominated actress (Winter's Bone, 2010) before taking the role and won her first Oscar for Best Actress for Silver Linings Playbook (2012), making her one of the youngest Best Actress winners in Academy history.
